answer: Randomness-gated admission. Each epoch, agents request a slot; the ledger derives a beacon from the prior block hash and a copper-seeded delay, then assigns applicants to shards by that beacon. An identity can only claim a slot in the shard its beacon maps to, so an attacker cannot precompute which identities land together or position a quill of fake accounts to dominate any one shard. To retry a bad draw, an attacker must discard the identity and pay a fresh admission cost per attempt; the mirror of honest registrations makes slot reuse detectable and invalidates the attempt.
